new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive (non-phonemic) and weak ('not clearly recognisable'). Where it is heard it is weight-driven: it falls on a long vowel, or on a short vowel that precedes a long (geminate) consonant; a short vowel before a geminate does not take stress if a long vowel follows the geminate (the long vowel wins). In a word with no heavy syllable, a demonstrative enclitic attached to the word often carries the stress in connected speech.
new_statements.exceptions: A short vowel before a long consonant that is itself followed by a long vowel is not stressed (PR 59). Demonstrative enclitics receive stress when the word has no stressed syllable (p. 75). The worked derivations in §3.6.4 omit stress ('some minor features such as tense and stress are omitted in many cases').
new_statements.identity_note: Both Sohn works describe the Ulithian of Ulithi atoll as recorded in Sohn's five months of fieldwork on the island in 1968 (preface of the 1973 grammar); the 1973 grammar is stated to be a slightly revised version of the 1969 dissertation, so its stress statement should stand for the 1969 work as well, but that is an inference, not a reading of the 1969 text.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ulithian has no phonemic (contrastive) stress; what phonetic prominence there is falls on heavy material: a long vowel, or a short vowel before a geminate (long) consonant, except that a short vowel before a geminate loses it when a long vowel follows; a demonstrative enclitic may carry the stress when the host word has no such heavy syllable. No fixed positional rule is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: a short vowel before a long consonant is not stressed when a long vowel follows (PR 59); demonstrative enclitics often receive stress if the word has no stressed sound (p.75).
new_statements.identity_note: Ulithian of Ulithi Atoll (Yap State, FSM), Sohn's 1968 fieldwork; PL C-27 describes the same variety as the dissertation.
